sources.authors: Cogitate Consortium (Ferrante O, Gorska-Klimowska U, Henin S, et al.)
sources.title: Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness
sources.relevance: Core source: adversarial collaboration testing both IIT and GWT predictions in 256 participants (fMRI+MEG+iEEG). The primary empirical foundation of today's article.
key_findings: IIT P1 (posterior content decoding) partially supported: ~95% iEEG, ~75% fMRI; adding PFC did not improve accuracy
IIT P2 (sustained posterior activity) failed: only 3.8% of posterior electrodes (25/657) showed sustained duration-tracking
IIT P3 (posterior gamma synchrony) failed: connectivity was brief <0.75s, low-frequency 2-25Hz, not gamma
GWT P1 (PFC content decoding) weakly supported: ~70% face-object decoding, only 0.2-0.4s window, no orientation/identity
GWT P2 (offset ignition) completely failed: 0/655 PFC iEEG electrodes showed predicted pattern (BF01=1.94×10⁴)
GWT P3 (long-range gamma sync) mixed: found some connectivity but low-frequency, not gamma-specific
Confirmed: conscious stimuli triggered brain-wide activation and synchronization (consistent with GWT's global broadcast)

sources.authors: Naccache L, Dehaene S, Changeux JP
sources.title: GNW theoretical framework and the 'adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness'
sources.relevance: GNW proponents' response to COGITATE. Provides the key arguments for why COGITATE does not falsify GWT.
key_findings: COGITATE confirmed non-trivial GWT prediction: brain-wide activation even without task relevance
Offset ignition was never a core GNWT prediction — only predicted when participants consciously attend to stimulus offset
PFC decoding difficulties reflect lack of columnar organization, not absence of information
COGITATE only used suprathreshold stimuli — cannot test GNWT's most central prediction (conscious vs unconscious processing contrast)

sources.title: Experimental and theoretical approaches to conscious processing
sources.relevance: Foundational GWT/GNWT review. Three neural signatures of consciousness: P3, late cortical amplification, long-range gamma synchrony. Time profile of ignition.

sources.authors: Koch C, Massimini M, Boly M, Tononi G
sources.title: Neural correlates of consciousness: progress and problems
sources.relevance: Foundational NCC framework review. Introduces content-specific NCC, full NCC, enabling NCC distinction. PCHZ hypothesis.

sources.authors: Boly M, Massimini M, Tsuchiya N, Postle BR, Koch C, Tononi G
sources.title: Are the neural correlates of consciousness in the front or in the back of the cerebral cortex? Clinical and neuroimaging evidence
sources.relevance: Evidence for posterior hot zone: bilateral frontal lobe removal doesn't affect consciousness; posterior lesions have 214-fold risk of vegetative state; no-report paradigms show posterior > prefrontal correlates.
